title: Control Flow, Functions and Errors
story: Programs need to choose, repeat and fail politely.
goal: Learn if, for, functions and Go's way of returning errors.

tests.label: Finish every try-it and quick check

hints: Read each block, then do the TRY IT and QUICK CHECK parts.
Every interactive block must be done to finish the lesson.
Take your time. Nothing here is timed.
socratic: Compare your result with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the most useful thing you learned here?

blocks.text: Go has one loop keyword, `for`. Functions can return more than one value, and errors are just values you check.

blocks.title: A function that can fail

blocks.q: How does a Go function usually report failure?
blocks.why: Go returns an error as the last result and the caller checks it with `if err != nil`.
Go has only one loop keyword: for.
